title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞} over Q, with the S_3 action permuting the three punctures. The quotient stack (U_{0,3}, S_3) is identified with M'_{1,1,Q}, the j-line stack. Up to the generic ±1 this is M_{1,1}, since λ-line/S_3 = j-line.

M is the lattice H_1(U_{0,3}(C), Z) = Z^3/Z(1,1,1), carrying the permutation action of S_3. This is my identification, based on the vanishing claims and the Fermat-tower context. Its completion is M̂ = M ⊗ Ẑ(1) = π_1^ab(U_{0,3,Q̄}), on which Π_Q acts through the cyclotomic character.

Theorem (bottom of p.716, top of this page). There is a profinite étale pro-cover U_∞ of the stack (U_{0,3,Q}, S_3) whose inverse image in U_{0,3,Q̄}, forgetting the S_3 action, is 'the' universal cover. The previous page says 'absolu universel', but the context points to the universal abelian cover, i.e. the Fermat tower with group M̂. Any two such pro-covers are related by a unique isomorphism.

In group terms, U_∞ corresponds to a splitting of 1 → M̂ → E → Π_Q × S_3 → 1. Here E is the quotient of π_1(M'_{1,1,Q}) by the kernel of π̂_1(U_{0,3,Q̄}) → M̂. Splittings are taken modulo M̂-conjugation.

Existence. Grothendieck notes two independent constructions:
- the Fermat tower x^n + y^n = z^n, which carries an action of (μ_n^3/μ_n) ⋊ S_3 defined over Q;
- the general theory of §49 VI.
Each gives a U_∞ unique up to unique isomorphism, so the question is whether they coincide.

Uniqueness. Two descents differ by a class in H^1(Π_Q × S_3, M̂), and automorphisms lie in H^0, which is 0. Use Hochschild–Serre for Π_Q × S_3.
- E_2^{1,0} = H^1(S_3, H^0(Π_Q, M̂)) = 0, because Ẑ(1)^{Π_Q} = 0.
- E_2^{0,1} = H^0(S_3, H^1(Π_Q, M̂)). By Kummer theory, H^1(Π_Q, M̂) = M ⊗ H^1(Π_Q, Ẑ(1)) = M ⊗ (Q*)^.
- These are the 'big' H^1 he says he was afraid of ('j'avais peur des gros H^1'). They are irrelevant, because M is Z-free with a trivial-action coefficient group A. The universal coefficient sequence 0 → H^0(S_3, M) ⊗ A → H^0(S_3, M ⊗ A) → Tor(H^1(S_3, M), A) → 0 shows that H^0(S_3, M) = H^1(S_3, M) = 0 forces H^0(S_3, M ⊗ A) = 0.
- Hence H^1(Π_Q × S_3, M̂) = 0 'sans rien connaître sur Π_Q'.

The S_3 vanishing (296) was obtained on p.716 from the splitting and rigidity of an extension of S_3 by M. Direct check on Z^3/Z(1,1,1):
- The invariants are 0.
- For H^1: Shapiro gives H^1(S_3, Z^3) = H^1(S_2, Z) = 0. The map H^2(S_3, Z) = Z/2 → H^2(S_2, Z) = Z/2 is restriction of the sign character, hence injective. So H^1 = 0.

Consequence. The Fermat-tower descent and the §49 VI descent coincide canonically. The next page uses this to interpret arithmetically the homomorphism M → G_{ρ,σ} ≅ Ẑ*·S^+ obtained algebraically in section 11°.
errors: No mathematical error found. The step from H^i(S_3,M)=0 (i=0,1) to H^0(S_3, M⊗(Q*)^)=0 is left implicit. It needs M to be Z-free and the coefficient group to carry trivial S_3-action; then universal coefficients apply. This matters because (Q*)^ has torsion (−1).
Also implicit: the vanishing of E_2^{1,0}, which follows from H^0(Π_Q, Ẑ(1))=0.

'le revêtement absolu universel' on p.716 should, from the Fermat-tower context and the abelian coefficient M̂, be the universal abelian cover. For the full nonabelian universal cover, an abelian H^1 alone would not settle uniqueness.

ideas.what: S_3-equivariant descent of the maximal abelian pro-cover of P^1−{0,1,∞} (the Fermat tower) to Q, as a pro-cover of the stack [U_{0,3}/S_3] = M'_{1,1}, unique up to unique isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Fermat tower as Galois/S_3-equivariant metabelian-level cover; descent of covers to the moduli stack M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fermat tower and Galois action: Ihara (1986, 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'), Anderson, Coleman; S_3-symmetry is classical
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as I know (unsure)

ideas.what: Uniqueness via Hochschild–Serre for Π_Q×S_3 with coefficients M⊗Ẑ(1): the S_3-cohomology vanishing kills the big Kummer group M⊗(Q*)^ with no arithmetic input
ideas.modern_name: Hochschild–Serre plus universal coefficients; rigidity of descent data

ideas.what: Computation H^0 = H^1 = 0 for S_3 acting on H_1(P^1−3 pts) = Z^3/Z
ideas.modern_name: cohomology of S_3 with coefficients in the reduced permutation lattice

missed.claim: An explicit canonical-rigidity statement: the abelian universal cover of U_{0,3,Q̄} has a unique-up-to-unique-isomorphism model over the j-line stack M'_{1,1,Q}. As a consequence, the Fermat tower and the abstract §49 VI construction agree canonically. The argument needs nothing about Gal(Q̄/Q).
missed.quote: c'est la nullité de H^i(S_3, M) pour i=0,1 qui implique (sans rien connaître sur Π_Q!) celle de H^1(Π_Q×S_3, M̂), qui assure l'unicité qu'il nous fallait
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a clean S_3-equivariant rigidity statement for the metabelian/Fermat level of the Galois action on π_1(P^1−3 pts). It is relevant to Ihara–Anderson–Coleman style results and the GT/Ihara program. The literature uses the Fermat tower but rarely phrases its canonicity as descent to M_{1,1} with an H^1 vanishing. The result itself is elementary, though.

missed.claim: The link between this arithmetic-geometric U_∞ and the purely algebraic homomorphism M → G_{ρ,σ} ≅ Ẑ*·S^+ of section 11° (developed on the next page) is part of an unpublished treatment. That treatment relates the Fermat tower to his combinatorial/Teichmüller-type groups.
missed.quote: Nous avons obtenu l'existence de deux façons : par la tour de Fermat et par la théorie générale du §49 VI
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may document how Grothendieck connected the abelian level of the Teichmüller tower to Fermat curves. That is of mostly historical interest, since Ihara's work covers the arithmetic substance.

deep.surprise_reason: The theorem and the proof are correct and neat, but the cohomological argument is routine, and the Fermat tower's Galois/S_3 structure is well studied (Ihara, Anderson). The canonical descent to M'_{1,1} is a nice unpublished formulation rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'j'avais pour des "gens"' should read 'j'avais peur des "gros" H^1(Π_Q, M̂)'.
'T_ℓ(G_m)' is probably T(G_m), the full Tate module Ẑ(1), not ℓ-adic. The underbraced H^1(Π_Q, T(G_m)) is annotated as the completion (Q*)^.
'pro-étales[?]' at the top may be 'revêtements profinis/pro-étales'; the meaning is the same.
On the previous page, 'revêtement absolu universel' is likely 'revêtement abélien universel', given the Fermat-tower context.
